Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I attached a first-pass commit proposal and a simple monthly ramp table that maps to your projected traffic for the next 12 months. Key points in the attachment:

- Base monthly commit (month 1-3): 1.2B input+output tokens/month
- Step-up schedule: increase to 2.5B in month 4 and 4.5B in month 8 to support your Q4 launch

A couple items we flagged for negotiation: whether the step-up commits can be front-loaded (larger early ramp) and whether we should include a price-protection clause in case you exceed the top tier.

Can you confirm the expected month-by-month ramp in the spreadsheet and call out any procurement constraints (billing cadence, PO timing)? If this looks good I can loop in finance for formal contract language.

Hi Rafael — thanks for the detailed proposal and the spreadsheet. A few initial questions from our side:

1) Step-up timing: RetailX will likely need a more aggressive ramp in month 3 to hit our beta launch. Can you support an accelerated step-up (1.2B -> 3.0B starting month 3) and still keep the same per-token bands?

2) Price protection: What happens if volume increases above the top tier (5B)? Do we get volume discounts retroactively for that month or a credit applied to future months?

3) Seasonality: We have a big promotional window in Nov that could exceed commits by ~40% for that month. Is there a way to accommodate a one-month spike without triggering overage charges or re-negotiation?

4) Contract mechanics: Procurement will require monthly invoicing and a 30-day net term. Also, we prefer step-ups to be locked by calendar month — any changes must be communicated 14 days prior.

Can you put together options (accelerated step-up + price protection clause + one-month spike handling) and include legal/finance-friendly language? Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Elena
Director, Product Partnerships, RetailX
elena@retailx.com

Rafael / team / Elena — quick pricing and ops note:

1) Accelerated step-up: we can support front-loading the ramp to hit 3.0B in month 3 assuming the customer accepts a slightly higher early-month ramp commitment profile. Operationally this increases baseline reserved capacity earlier, but we can enable a 4-week warm-up buffer in month 2 to smooth cache/throughput. Pricing: keep the same per-token bands but apply a temporary 5% uplift on months 1-3 for making capacity available earlier (this is negotiable).

2) Above-top-tier treatment (volume >5B): two options we typically offer:
   - Retroactive tiering: apply the next tier discount to the entire month's usage if month usage exceeds 5B (subject to a 2% reconciliation fee), OR
   - Overage credit: bill at overage rate (slightly higher) and issue a credit the next month equal to difference up to a cap.

3) One-month spike handling: recommend a "spike bucket" equal to 25% of committed volume for 1 month at no extra charge, plus an option to pre-purchase additional spike capacity at the top tier price. For a 40% spike we can cover 25% free and propose a capped overage rate on the remaining 15% or encourage a short-term top-up commit for that month.

4) Billing terms: Monica? From product ops perspective we can do monthly invoicing net-30; finance will want an initial PO and legal signature.

Specific suggested language for the contract (draft):
"Customer may increase committed monthly volume with 14 days' notice. For any calendar month in which Customer's metered usage exceeds the Top Tier threshold, Redwood will either (a) apply retroactive tier pricing to the month's total usage at Redwood's discretion, subject to a reconciliation fee, or (b) bill overages at the agreed overage rate and issue a credit in the following invoice equal to the delta up to a defined cap. Additionally, Customer is entitled to one (1) one-month spike allowance equal to 25% of committed volume per contract year. Any residual spike beyond the allowance will be billed at the overage rate unless Customer prepays a temporary increased commit for that month."

Happy to iterate on wording. Rafael, if Elena is okay with the 5% early-ramp uplift we can present a clean option A (no uplift) and option B (5% uplift + guaranteed month-3 ramp).

— Ben

Subject: Re: RetailX questions — billing and legal constraints

Rafael / team / Elena — from finance/legal side:

- Net-30 monthly invoicing: acceptable. We require a PO for the initial month and standard credit checks for monthly billing.
- Price protection clause: we prefer the retroactive tiering mechanism as it maps cleanly to billing reconciliation. If retroactive tiering applied, we will limit reconciliation to 60 days after invoice and apply a 2% processing fee on reconciled amounts.
- Spike allowance: we can approve a 25% one-month spike allowance per contract year. For spikes >25% we will support either a pre-paid temporary uplift or bill at the pre-agreed overage rate; credits for overages will be processed on the next invoice cycle.
- Contract amendment: step-ups that materially change committed spend will require an amendment; small front-loaded ramps that remain within the contract's overall 12-month committed spend are manageable with an amendment note.

If RetailX accepts retroactive tiering and monthly net-30 terms, finance can draft the billing section and hand it to legal for redline.

— Monica
Finance Ops, Redwood Inference

- Tiered per-token discounts at 1B, 2.5B, 5B monthly thresholds; overages billed at agreed overage rate
- 25% one-month spike allowance per contract year

Option B (accelerated ramp — recommended if you need beta launch coverage):
- Front-loaded ramp to 3.0B starting month 3; Redwood applies a 5% early-ramp uplift on months 1-3 to cover reserved capacity; thereafter standard tiered pricing
- Retroactive tiering for months >5B with a 2% reconciliation fee OR alternative overage-credit model (we can choose)
- 25% one-month spike allowance; remaining spike billed at overage rate or via short-term pre-purchase
- Monthly invoicing, Net-30; PO and initial credit check

Next steps: please confirm which option you prefer (A or B) and whether you want retroactive tiering or the overage-credit model.
